text: MIDNIGHT TO-NIGHT!

label: text
text: Warning to Big Shipping.

label: text
text: TRACK OF THE STORM: A STEAMER'S

label: text
text: Hong Kong, it seems, will have to be resigned to a typhoon during October bank-holiday week-end. The experts say that the cyclone is coming this way and have issued a warning to shipping.

label: text
text: Midnight to-night is the time preached when cyclone is expected to pass to the south of Gap Rock, or roughly 50 miles from the Colony.

label: text
text: The typhoon passed a few miles south of Pratas at 6 a.m. on a west-north-west track.

label: text
text: It is most likely to pass south of Gap Rock at about midnight or a little later.

label: text
text: The wind at Gap Rock is north-north-west, forre 8 (which is ash gule" according to the aufort scale), for the last 12 hours, and is likely to increase as the typhoon approaches.

label: text
text: The typhoon passed over the Java "Lijin" s.s. "Tjiliwong" at 8 p.m. last night, in Lat. 19N., Long. 118½E. Her barometer was falling at 28.55.

label: text
text: The barometer at the Royal Observatory, Kowloon, is at present 29.69, falling slowly.

label: text
text: A strong gale is also reported in the Formosa Channel.

label: text
text: At Hong Kong the gale will probably commence from the north and veer to north-east and east.

label: text
text: About 11 a.m. the Observatory issued the following warning:—It is very dangerous for ocean-going vessels to leave Hong Kong at present.

label: text
text: The position of the typhoon at present is 150 miles south of Hong Kong.

label: text
text: Yesterday evening, No. 1 signal gave place to No. 2 (gale expected from the north).

label: text
text: Small craft went to shelter behind the Causeway Bay and Yaumati breakwaters.

label: text
text: The Government rescue lug

label: text
text:
Ocean-going steamers left the Kowloon wharves last night and went to typhoon moorings.
A few of the river steamboats also took shelter but services this morning to Macao and Canton left as usual.

label: text
text: It was also noticed that although there was a blow in the harbour, quite a number of the smaller coasting boats were still at their buoys.

label: text
text: As the day progressed, a good many left for Kowloon Bay and the seclusion of behind Stone cutters Island.

label: text
text: In town the blow was not particularly noticeable. But on the Peak and on the Praya, a stiff breeze, approaching a moderate gale, was blowing.

label: text
text: It is thought that the typhoon—unless it swerves—will be felt at its height to-nigh and that the storm will be over by tomorrow night.

label: paragraph_title
text: POSTAL INSURANCE.

label: text
text:
IMPORTANT REGULATIONS
AMENDED.

label: text
text: The regulations made by the Governor in Council under section 3 of the Post Office Ordinance, 1926, on June 24, 1926, have been amended by the rescission of regulation 26 and the substitution of the following regulation therefor:—

label: text
text: "Registered letters and parcels may be insured up to the limits stated in the Postal Guide for letters and in the Appendix to these Regulations for parcels. The fee for insurance of letters shall be 20 cents for each 300 francs (or £12 or $120) or part thereof. The fee for insurance of parcels shall be 25 cents for each 300 francs (or £12 or $120) or part thereof. The right to insure and the right to compensate in case of loss or damage shall be subject in all respects to the provisions of the Postal Guide. In this regulation 'Postal Guide' means the Postal Guide issued by the Postmaster General and current at the time of insuring or claiming as the case may be."

label: text
text: The resolution of the Miners' Delegate Conference yesterday, in favour of intensifying the coal dispute, imposes a difficult task upon the Miners' Executive. It is generally agreed that if instructional are given immediately to withdraw the safety men the response will be doubtful. "Anyhow the Miners' Federation controls only a proportion of safety men. In other organisations the safety men, including those of the South Wales Colliery dad Craftsmen's Association comprising sixty per cent of the safety men of South Wales, have already announced that they will remain at work. It is pointed out that the Federation has already vainly tried to secure an embargo on the import of foreign coal and the Trades Union Congress has decided that to make a levy on other Unions is impracticable.—Reuter.
